question.leadin: Answer the following about emperors of Japan.
question.text: This man has the distinction of maintaining the longest reign of any Japanese emperor. He is more famously known for overseeing the Japanese surrender during World War II.
question.clue: The empowerment of this man was the state goal of the League of Blood, while the year of his ascension saw a financial crisis triggered by the devaluation of Earthquake Bonds, leading to the rise of conglomerate control of the economy.

swap.leadin: The final holder of this title was Tokugawa Yoshinobu.
swap.text: Prior to an 1868 restoration of imperial rule, what title was held by military rulers of Japan?
swap.clue: A power vacuum created after the death of a holder of this title led to the Onin War, which initiated the Sengoku period.

question.leadin: Saigo Takamori was an influential member of this class.
question.text: Name this class of warrior nobility from feudal Japan. Members of this class traditionally carried both a long katana and a shorter sword.
question.clue: Members of this group could find a job by embarking on a type of pilgrimage called musha shugyo, and their only goal should be "to grasp the long and the short swords and to die".

swap.leadin: Holders of this title, which originated in the Heian (hay-ahn) period, ruled from the Bakufu.
swap.text: Holding power until the 1867 Meiji (may-jee) Restoration, name this title that denoted military rulers of Japan such as Ashikaga Takauji.
swap.clue: After the arrival of the "black ships," the isolationist rule of this office was ended with the Convention of Kanagawa, shortly before they were made obsolete with the Meiji Restoration.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the restoration of the Meiji ["may-jee's"] Emperor's power.
question.text: This declaration was issued by the Meiji Emperor after he took the throne. "Evil customs of the past" were done away with after this document was issued, as it paved the way for the westernization of Japan.
question.answerHtml: Charter Oath [or Gokajo no Goseimon; or the Oath in Five Articles]
question.clue: This document officially ceded power to Emperor Meiji whose third clause allowed the ability to pursue any occupation regardless of social standing.

swap.text: This daimyo preceded Toyotomi Hideyoshi as the first "great unifier." He was killed in 1582 when his retainer Akechi Mitsuhide ["mit-soo-hee-day"] rebelled against him.
swap.clue: This huge fan of the Tanegashima rifle once won a battle by arranging his arquebusiers into three rows.

question.text: Although the shogunate was centered on Kamakura, the official capital and residence of the emperor remained this western city, whose name simply means "capital city."
question.clue: Henry Stimson, the US Secretary of War, is said to have honeymooned here, and famously lobbied to have this city taken off the list of bombing targets during the Second World War despite significant protests from the military.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Hojo clan.
swap.text: The Hojo were the effective rulers during this shogunate named for a city that's today famous for a large Buddha statue. This shogunate took power after the Heian period.
swap.clue: Before a major battle one leader of this polity meditated to find the source of cowardice in himself, and one conflict during it occurred when the cloistered emperor Go-Toba attempted to take the throne.

question.leadin: During this era, a period of economic expansion and the flourishing of the arts took place in its Genroku Period.
question.text: Identify this government that was ended by an era of rapid industrialization called the Meiji restoration. Ieyasu was its first leader.
question.answerHtml: Tokugawa Shogunate [or Tokugawa Period; or Edo Period; or Tokugawa Bafuku; or Edo Bafuku]
question.clue: Its downfall came during the Bakamatsu, during which popular sentiment called for "expelling the barbarians", leading to the Boshin War and resignation of Yoshinobu.

swap.leadin: How many capitals of Japan are there? Only one. Nevertheless, there have been many ancient capitals of Japan.
swap.text: This city names a period following the Asuka and was the first Japanese capital built in the Tang Chinese style. It was also the first permanent capital of Japan, before Nagaoka.
swap.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

question.leadin: Identify the following about a nation's history.
question.text: During the Muromachi period this clan held the shogunate. Members included Takauji and Yoshimitsu.
question.clue: A ruler of this family promoted the "Higashiyama culture" of the eastern hills, which popularized shoin ("sho-een") homes with tatami floors; his aesthetic was exemplified by the "wabi-sabi" style of a temple that he couldn't afford to coat in silver.

swap.text: Ieyasu became undisputed shogun after defeating his rivals at this 1600 engagement.
swap.clue: The capture of Konosu and Gifu Castles preceded this battle, whose decisive moment saw a staged round of arquebus fire signal a force of turncoats to attack the army of their initial ally Otani instead.

question.text: The importance placed on the renunciation of imperial divinity is noted in this 1999 book by John W. Dover that explores the occupation and democratization of Japan after World War II.

swap.leadin: During one of these events, soldiers fought on and around large walls at Iki-no-matsubara, and before these events a letter was sent addressed to the "ruler of a small country."
swap.text: Name these events chronicled by Suenaga, the second of which was repelled by a fleet-crushing "divine wind."
swap.answerHtml: Mongol invasions of Japan [or Yuan invasions of Japan; or Kublai Khan’s invasions of Japan; accept equivalents for invasion like “attack”; prompt on “Chinese invasion of Japan”; prompt on “invasions of Japan”]
swap.clue: During one of these conflicts, an exaggerated 142,000-strong army was defeated at the battle of Hakata Bay.

question.leadin: Ka'en jars, with tops that resemble flames, were principally produced during the middle of this period.
question.text: Name this period, which gets its name from using rope to make marks on pottery. The Yayoi culture succeeded this period.
question.clue: This period's namesake hunter-gatherers were supplanted by the agricultural Yayoi ] people.

swap.leadin: This mastermind of this event was killed at the subsequent Battle of Yamazaki.
swap.text: Name this event in which Akechi Mitsuhide betrayed the first of the three Great Unifiers of Japan and drove him to commit suicide.
swap.answerHtml: Honno-Ji Incident [or Honno-ji no hen; prompt on “Kyoto” siege; prompt, BUT DO NOT SAY, things like “Oda Nobunaga’s death/suicide/killing”]
swap.clue: This event in which a Japanese warlord committed seppuku after being ambushed during a tea ceremony. Its instigator, Akechi Mitsuhide, was later defeated at the Battle of Yamazaki by the forces of Toyotomi Hideyoshi.

question.leadin: Emperor Kotoku implemented this set of policies, which included the abolition of private landholding and a tax based on population instead of land use.
question.text: Name this 645 A.D. set of centralizing reforms inspired by Tang Dynasty China, which brought Japan under the control of the imperial court.
question.answerHtml: Taika Reforms [or Taika no Kaishin; or Great Reformation of the Taika Era]
question.clue: This set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.

swap.leadin: A legend claims this man had his retainer Katakura Kojuro gouge out his right eye, so that the enemy couldn't take it from him, and therefore he was known as the "one-eyed dragon."
swap.text: Name this daimyo who founded the city of Sendai and sent his retainer Hasekura Tsunenaga on a diplomatic mission to the Vatican on the ship the San Juan Batista.
swap.clue: This daimyo frequently called the "one-eyed dragon" because he lost an eye to smallpox.

question.text: In 1580, Oda Nobunaga destroyed this sect of fanatical Buddhist monks during a campaign that included the brutal massacre at Mount Hiei. They often used nembutsu to strike fear into their enemies.
question.clue: Rennyo eventually tried to distance himself from these groups, who had organized to defend him against aggression from Enryaku-ji.

swap.leadin: Takeda Katsuyori instigated, and ultimately lost, this battle when he legendarily failed to heed his father's advice that "a mountain does not move."
swap.text: Name this battle where the Takeda clan was defeated at a namesake castle by ashigaru infantry using European-style matchlock arquebus rifles.
swap.clue: Fearing a repeat of the events of Mikatagahara, one side's commander built a series of zigzagging wooden stockades and deployed his arquebusiers behind them.
